evaluation:
Helpful Facts:

  • Headache Characteristics: Reports severe, throbbing (pulsating), unilateral headaches.
  • Location: Pain localized to the temporal region and retro-orbital area.
  • Severity: Intense pain.
  • Frequency: Approximately 3-4 times per week.
  • Duration: Several hours, sometimes lasting the entire day (consistent with 4-72 hour migraine duration).
  • Aggravating Factors: Symptoms exacerbated by physical activity, bright lights (photophobia), loud noises (phonophobia), and strong odors.
  • Associated Symptoms: Nausea, fatigue, intermittent neck stiffness.
  • Aura: Reports intermittent visual aura (flashing lights or zigzags) preceding headache onset.
  • Behavioral Response: Attempts to alleviate symptoms by resting in a dark, quiet room.
  • Pertinent Negatives: Denies fever, neurological deficits, recent illnesses, recent head/neck injuries.
  • Medication History: Denies trying OTC or prescription medications for these headaches. Confirms adherence to Fluoxetine.
  • Relevant History: History of depression (a common comorbidity with migraine).

What wasn't covered but would be helpful:

  • Family History: No information on family history of headaches or migraine.
  • Previous Headache History: No information on whether the patient has experienced similar headaches in the past, even if not diagnosed as migraine.
  • Detailed Aura Description: While aura is mentioned, details like duration of aura, progression (e.g., scintillating scotoma), and whether it includes sensory or motor symptoms are missing.
  • Triggers: While stress was denied, exploration of other potential triggers (e.g., specific foods, alcohol, caffeine, sleep changes, hormonal changes/menstrual cycle if applicable) is missing.
  • Associated Symptoms (Further Detail): Specific questions about vomiting, prodromal symptoms (e.g., mood changes, yawning, food cravings), or postdromal symptoms (e.g., feeling drained) were not asked.
  • Impact on Function: Information on how these headaches affect the patient's daily activities (work, social life, etc.) is missing.
  • Menstrual History (if applicable): For female patients, the relationship between headache onset/severity and the menstrual cycle is crucial information.
  • Social History Details: Specifics on caffeine intake, alcohol consumption, and smoking status are missing, as these can be relevant triggers or confounders.
  • Review of Systems (More Comprehensive): While some negatives were included, a more thorough ROS focusing on potential secondary headache causes (e.g., sinus symptoms, dental pain, vision changes beyond aura) would be beneficial.
